mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of dissolved substances in conductivity
mcqs.question: Which of the following best explains why a liquid can conduct electricity?

options.A: The liquid contains dissolved substances that produce free ions
options.B: The liquid is at a high temperature
options.C: The liquid is exposed to bright light
options.D: The liquid has suspended solid particles

mcqs.answer: The liquid contains dissolved substances that produce free ions
mcqs.explanation: Conductivity in liquids depends on the presence of charged particles. When a substance such as salt dissolves, it separates into ions that can move and carry electric current. Temperature, light, or suspended solids do not create charge carriers, so they do not make a liquid conductive.

mcqs.learning_point: Use simple circuits to test conductivity
mcqs.question: In a simple circuit consisting of a battery, a bulb and two wires, which observation shows that the liquid being tested conducts electricity?
mcqs.explanation: When the liquid conducts, it completes the circuit allowing current to flow, which makes the bulb light. An off bulb means the circuit is open; heating of the battery or melting wires are not typical indicators of conductivity in a simple test.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches a conducting liquid with a non‑conducting liquid?
mcqs.explanation: Salt water contains dissolved ions and conducts electricity, whereas distilled water lacks ions and does not conduct. The other pairs either both conduct or both do not, or are not clear distinctions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that some liquids conduct electricity
mcqs.question: A student connects a bulb to a battery and places the electrodes in three separate liquids. The bulb lights up in liquid A, stays off in liquid B, and flickers in liquid C. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Liquid A contains dissolved ions that allow current flow
options.B: Liquid B is a strong electrolyte
options.C: Liquid C is a pure metal

mcqs.answer: Liquid A contains dissolved ions that allow current flow
mcqs.explanation: The bulb lighting indicates a complete circuit via ions in liquid A. An off bulb (liquid B) suggests no ions, and flickering (liquid C) may indicate intermittent contact, not a reliable conductor. Hence only liquid A is confirmed as a conductor.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a conducting liquid?
mcqs.explanation: Conducting liquids contain free ions; salt water, lemon juice, and copper sulfate solution all have ions. Pure distilled water lacks dissolved ions, so it does not conduct electricity, correcting the common misconception that all liquids conduct.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of dissolved substances in conductivity
mcqs.question: Why does adding common salt (NaCl) to water increase the water's ability to conduct electricity?

options.A: The salt dissociates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that can move and carry charge
options.B: The salt raises the temperature of the water
options.C: The salt makes the water more viscous, allowing better flow of electrons
options.D: The salt changes the colour of the water, indicating conductivity

mcqs.answer: The salt dissociates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that can move and carry charge
mcqs.explanation: When NaCl dissolves, it separates into positively and negatively charged ions. These ions are the charge carriers that enable electric current. Temperature, viscosity, and colour have no direct effect on electrical conductivity in this context.

mcqs.learning_point: Use simple circuits to test conductivity
mcqs.question: When testing an unknown liquid for conductivity, which method provides the most quantitative result?

options.A: Connecting a bulb in series with the liquid and observing whether it lights
options.B: Using a multimeter to measure the resistance of the liquid
options.C: Observing if the liquid changes colour when electrodes are inserted
options.D: Listening for a faint spark when the electrodes touch the liquid

mcqs.answer: Using a multimeter to measure the resistance of the liquid
mcqs.explanation: A multimeter gives a numerical resistance value, allowing precise comparison of conductivity. A bulb only shows a qualitative yes/no result, while colour change or sparks are not reliable quantitative measures.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly explains why pure ethanol does not conduct electricity, whereas a solution of sodium chloride in water does?

options.A: Ethanol lacks free ions, while NaCl solution provides mobile ions
options.B: Ethanol has a higher viscosity than the NaCl solution
options.C: The NaCl solution is at a higher temperature than ethanol
options.D: Ethanol contains metallic particles that block charge flow

mcqs.answer: Ethanol lacks free ions, while NaCl solution provides mobile ions
mcqs.explanation: Electrical conduction in liquids requires charge carriers. Pure ethanol consists of neutral molecules and has no ions, so it cannot conduct. Dissolving NaCl in water produces Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that move under an electric field, enabling conduction. Viscosity, temperature, or metallic particles are irrelevant here.
